title: Workplace Cafe Management Program: Termination and Exit Terms
content:
**Clause — who may terminate.** Only the client may terminate a cafe management contract issued under the Workplace Cafe Management Program. Termination begins with the client's own written notice; it is never begun by anything the desk itself does on the client's behalf.

**Clause — when notice is handled.** Notice is handled only on a contract that stands active, suspended, or already in transition out. Notice is never handled on a contract that is still proposed, still mobilizing, or already closed. Eligibility to have notice handled is read from the contract's own status on file, checked before the request is handled, and is read against the specific cafe contract named in the request rather than any other contract the same client may hold. Where the contract's status admits it, the desk records the request as a termination notice, held for the client to confirm.

**Clause — dating the closure.** A closure may not be dated earlier than the service model's termination notice period, counted in calendar days from the day the client gives written notice of termination. That notice day is the date on file for the contract's own termination notice — not a date the client separately recalls or states elsewhere. Notice days are counted as calendar days beginning the day after written notice is given; weekends and public holidays count toward the total. Where the day the count lands on is a date the month does not contain, the last day of that month is used instead. The boundary day itself — the final day of the counted notice period — is a day on which closure may be dated; a closure dated any day earlier fails the notice period.

*Hypothetical illustration only.* Suppose, purely for illustration, that the termination notice period printed against a service model were 30 calendar days and written notice were given on the 1st of a month. Counting begins on the 2nd. A closure dated the 31st — the 30th counted day — just satisfies the notice period; a closure dated the 30th — one day short — just fails it. This 30-day figure is illustrative only and is not the company's printed notice period for any service model.

**Clause — early exit charge — no longer in force.** The contract formerly stated that where the closure day fell before the end of the contracted term, the early exit charge was the number of monthly management fees printed against the service model, calculated on the fee in force on the notice day. That clause is no longer in force, superseded by the current basis; the number of monthly management fees printed against the service model for this purpose remains a figure of record and is not restated here as a number. Where the closure day falls on or after the end of the contracted term and the renewal notice was exchanged in time, no early exit charge falls due — this treatment remains in force.

**Clause — closure settlement — no longer in force.** The contract formerly stated that, on closure, the equipment deposit was returned net of any charge outstanding, drawable subsidy funding left on the contract was refunded to the client, and the final invoice settled the balance in one document. That clause is no longer in force, superseded by the current basis.

**Clause — proposals withdrawn before countersignature.** A proposal that never reached countersignature closes without notice, without an early exit charge, and without a final invoice. This treatment remains in force.

**Parameters printed per service model.** Each of the six service models of the Workplace Cafe Management Program prints its own termination notice period, in calendar days; its own count of monthly management fees charged on early exit; its own renewal notice period, in calendar days, by which renewal intentions must be exchanged; and its own standard initial contract term, in months. No single figure is shared across all six service models for any of these.

superseded_clauses: Where the closure day falls before the end of the contracted term, the early exit charge is the number of monthly management fees printed against the service model, calculated on the fee in force on the notice day.

On closure the equipment deposit is returned net of any charge outstanding, drawable subsidy funding left on the contract is refunded to the client, and the final invoice settles the balance in one document.
